nodes.title: Replay Pack: every selected photo as one set of references
Bake the cast into one RefCap (muted: Ctrl+M to run once)
Read me
widgets_values:
## 7. Two characters (and a place) in one shot
One RefCap holds one subject, so a scene with several characters takes **one *H3 RefCap Select* per file**, chained into
*H3 RefCap Replay Pack*. The replay is bit-identical to *MiniMax H3 Reference to Video* fed the same photos.

**Choosing**
- Press **Pick views...** on a Select node: a thumbnail browser of `models/refcaps` opens, showing the photos stored in
  each RefCap. Click the ones this shot needs; the footer counts images and reference tokens.
- Or type them: `all`, `none`, or 0-based numbers and ranges (`0,2,5-7`). `clips` and `audios` take 1-based numbers.
- The **Label guide** output lists which `<Picture i>` each photo became, in chain order. Write the prompt to match:
  `<Subject 1> is the woman in <Picture 1>, <Picture 2> and <Picture 3>` and so on. A location works the same way:
  `The location is the room in <Picture 7> and <Picture 8>.`

**Limits** (the reference node's, whatever the photos come from): **9 images, 3 clips, 3 audio references** per render.
Each photo costs about 196 reference tokens at `match` and 1,024 at `max`, on every sampling step.

**Bake** writes the current selection to one RefCap in `models/refcaps`, for a cast you keep reusing. It copies the
stored pixels and latents, so nothing is re-encoded — re-bake after re-capturing one of the sources.

**Measured** (lf_013 + lf_117, 3 seeds): two faces in 16/16 frames of every clip and never both matching the same
person; identity 0.35-0.50 in a medium two-shot, against ~0.63 for a single-character close-up. An environment
reference carried the sofa, lamp, bookshelf and rug of the room it was taken from.

**Settings in these workflows** follow ComfyUI's MiniMax H3 reference-to-video template: the ref2va model with its 4-step Lightning LoRA, 4 steps, `res_multistep` + `simple`, 608x352. For the base model, bypass the *Lightning LoRA* node and use 20 steps. The measurements quoted here ran on a community H3 turbo finetune (shift 6/3, 8 steps) on a 12 GB GPU. Raise the size and length for final renders; the reference tokens ride through every step, so more photos and larger captures cost time.

nodes.title: Prompt guide
widgets_values:
## Writing the prompt
H3's reference mode reads a structured prompt. The photos are labelled in order: `<Picture 1>` ... `<Picture N>`, where N is the number of photos in the RefCap.

```
subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is the woman in <Picture 1>, <Picture 2> and <Picture 3>, a white woman in her mid-twenties with dark brown, wavy, shoulder-length hair.

summary:
[reference generation] <Subject 1> sits at a sunlit cafe table and smiles at the camera.

retention_analysis:
<Subject 1> (appears in [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - the woman's facial identity and hairstyle are retained.

detailed_description:
The target video is a realistic, full-color cinematic shot with warm daylight.
[Shot 1] A medium close-up shows <Subject 1>, wearing a navy t-shirt, ...

overall_soundscape:
Gentle street ambience.

non_diegetic_music:
N/A
```

**Tips**
- Describe age, gender and hair, and **say the outfit and action you want**. The photos supply the face; the prompt supplies everything else.
- Don't count on a name. The tests never used one.
- More detail in `detailed_description` (camera, lighting, motion, sound) gives better shots. MiniMax's guide suggests 350-500 words for final renders.
- Official format guide: MiniMax-H3 `docs/VIDEO_PROMPT_WRITING_GUIDE_ref_en.md`.
